reply_text:
Now open the main pages.I found five candidates from 2011, all on pages I opened. Two match claims you've already recorded and three are new. Each comes from Legg's own blog or from a published email Q&A.

**New, not in your recorded list:**
1. **50% by 2028 (17 June 2011, LessWrong Q&A).** He was asked for the years by which he'd give 10%, 50% and 90% odds of human-level machine intelligence. He answered "2018, 2028, 2050". You've recorded the 10% and 90% parts but not the 50% one, which is the figure most often cited later.
2. **The 2025–2040 "theme" (31 January 2011, vetta.org post "Technological themes").** He wrote: "Thus my pick for the theme from 2025 to 2040 is machine intelligence." In a reply below the post on 4 February 2011, he said this would range from specialised machine-learning systems "to fledgeling AGIs."
3. **Mean of 2028 and most likely year 2025 (31 December 2011, vetta.org post "Goodbye 2011, hello 2012").** This is the same post as your recorded proto-AGI claim, but it's a separate statement: a log-normal spread for human-level AGI with a mean of 2028 and a mode (most likely year) of 2025. He made it on the condition that nothing like a nuclear war happens.

**Things to watch when checking:**
- The 31 December post is stamped "2:49 am" with no time zone. Comments on the post run from 31 December 2011 into January 2012, so later remarks on it don't belong to 2011.
- The LessWrong Q&A was done by email and published on 17 June 2011. The exact day Legg answered isn't shown.
- An interview by Jonathan Despres on the future.fandom.com wiki has dated claims: an AI boom around 2020, human-level AI passed in the mid-2020s, and things getting "really crazy" sometime from 2025 to 2040. The page carries no date and I couldn't find one, so I left it under other_years rather than as a 2011 candidate.
- I didn't count his Q6 answer ("my number 1 risk for this century") because it ranks risks rather than predicting something AI will do. His Q8 milestone answer has no date.
- My first tool call broke after the first fixed search had already run, so I reused that result rather than run it again. One page opening was refused, so I used 10 of 12 searches and 5 of 6 openings.
